newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu's first months as Israeli prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu's first months as Israeli prime minister.

text.p: Benjamin Netanyahu was narrowly elected Israel's prime minister on May 29, 1996. Here are some highlights of his first months in office:
June 18 - Netanyahu, right-wing Likud leader who ousted Labour party Prime Minister Shimon Peres, takes office promising to promote peace with Arab neighbours while ensuring security.
June 28 - Netanyahu sends representatives to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
July 23 - Arafat meets Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in Gaza in first high-level meeting since Netanyahu took office.
Aug 2 - Netanyahu infuriates Palestinians by lifting four-year freeze on Jewish settlement expansion in occupied West Bank imposed by the previous government.
Aug 9 - Israel says no progress on peace moves until Palestinian Authority shuts offices in Arab East Jerusalem.
Aug 25 - Bowing to Israeli demands, Arafat's Palestinian Authority shuts two East Jerusalem offices.
Aug 27 - Israel hoists bulldozer over Jerusalem's Old City wall to demolish Palestinian community centre said to have been built without permit.

Aug 29 - Palestinians hold first general strike in West Bank and Gaza in two years to protest at Israeli policy; heads of Israeli-PLO steering committee on implementing interim peace deals hold first meeting since Netanyahu took office.
Sept 4 - Netanyahu, Arafat hold first summit.
Sept 24 - Israel opens Jerusalem tourist tunnel near Islamic holy site, igniting protests and further souring relations with Arab states. Sixty-one Palestinians, 15 Israeli soldiers die.
Sept 29 - U.S. President Bill Clinton invites Netanyahu, Arafat, Jordan's King Hussein and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to White House summit.
Oct 6 - Following White House summit, Israel and PLO launch weeks of marathon talks on Hebron redeployment.
Dec 11 - Guerrillas from Popular Front for Liberation of Palestine shoot 12-year-old Israeli boy and his mother near PLO-ruled West Bank town of Ramallah.
Dec 12 - Israeli farmer shoots dead a Palestinian worker in southern Israel.
Dec 24 - Netanyahu, Arafat meet on Hebron. U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross reports progress.
Jan 1, 1997 - Off-duty Israeli soldier fires into market in West Bank town of Hebron, wounding seven Palestinians.
Jan 17 - PLO and Israel sign deal for Israeli withdrawal from most of Hebron.
Jan 19 - Arafat takes control of most of Hebron, telling Jewish settlers who remain in divided city he wants peace.
Feb 26 - Israeli committee approves building 6,500 homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem in defiance of world criticism.
March 13 - Seven Israeli schoolgirls gunned down by Jordanian soldier on border.
March 18 - Bulldozers break ground on new Jewish settlement, igniting Palestinian protests; five Palestinians killed by Israeli security forces and settlers.
March 21 - Moslem bomber kills himself, three Israelis in Tel Aviv cafe.
March 22 - Clashes flare in Hebron and militant Hamas group threatens more attacks against Jewish state.
April 7 - Netanyahu, Clinton hold crisis talks in Washington.
April 16 - Israeli police recommend indicting Netanyahu for fraud and breach of trust in political corruption scandal.
April 17 - Netanyahu refuses to quit.
April 20 - Attorney-general, citing insufficient evidence, says no changes will be filed against Netanyahu.
